chapters.chapter_key: water and intention: the anatomy of ablution
chapters.before_md:
I mention now the circumstances that make ablution (اَلْوُضُوء) necessary.

It is said in the book known as the Book of Question and Answer, arranged according to the order of the doors of Daaim al-Islam, the questions being those of certain teachers of the Indian lands and the answers those of the summoners of the Yemeni lands:

Question: What do you say, O best of those who have cast upon us the lights of his knowledge, regarding a matter over which our minds have labored? It has come in the Book of Purity that a man is forbidden to urinate beneath fruit-bearing trees. O our master, what is intended by these trees — those upon which fruit is actually present, or those whose property it is to bear fruit? Answer: The trees in which fruit is present, or those whose property it is to bear it.

Question: What do you say regarding what has come in the books of the dawah forbidding the greeting of one who is in a state of hadath, and forbidding speech in that state? O our master, if the one in that state rises from that place, having cleansed himself with a stone or with something else, is it permitted for him to speak, and is it permitted to greet him? Answer: Once he has risen, he may be greeted, and he must return the greeting and may speak.

Question: What does our master say regarding a stone or a clod of earth with which a man cleanses himself after urinating, which afterward dries, and which he then uses a second time — is that permitted? Answer: There is no harm in it, provided that no impurity and no moisture are evident upon it.

It is said in the book Mukhtasar al-Musannaf that what nullifies ablution is:

- Sleep
- Whatever issues from the front or rear passage, whether a stone or wind
- An enema
- Fainting
- Insanity
- The disappearance of the glans into the front passage of a living person or a dead one

It is said in the book Tawil al-Daaim that it has likewise come down that if one performing ablution interrupts it, he may build upon what he has already done, so long as the water has not dried upon the limbs already washed.

It is also said in Mukhtasar al-Musannaf that whoever has had both hands amputated above the elbows, so that nothing remains of them, the obligation of washing the hands has fallen away from him.

Our master and lord, the Trusted of the Imam, the Banner of Islam (رض), said in his gatherings entitled Majalis al-Bayan and Majalis al-Hikma, known as the Councils of al-Mustansiriyya, in the fifth council:

You have heard what was recited to you, wherein we singled you out with the splendid glad tidings and joined you to the company of those of whom God Almighty said:

> لَهُمُ ٱلْبُشْرَىٰ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَفِى ٱلْآخِرَةِ

Theirs are the glad tidings in the life of this world and in the hereafter.

We set forth the honoring of the number nineteen by its conjunction with the clauses of the testimony and its seven letters and its twelve, and that Islam is built upon the seven obligations, to which twelve practices are attached — in a manner not hidden from one who possesses knowledge and discernment. Listen now, then, to what is recited to you: that to every obligation among the obligations already mentioned there belong seven obligations and twelve practices. Among them is the walaya (الْوِلَايَة), which is the first and most excellent of them. It has been said before that in every allusion made by these numbers, the ranking of the friends of God is the utmost aim and intention.

After the walaya comes purity, and in it are seven obligations and twelve practices. The seven obligations are those of ablution, which is the lesser purity (الطَّهَارَةُ الصُّغْرَى):

1. Pure water
2. Intention
3. Washing the face
4. Washing the hands
5. Wiping the head
6. Wiping the feet
7. Order, which is that one begins with what God Almighty has begun by mentioning

The twelve practices are:

1. Cleansing oneself after relieving oneself (اَلِاسْتِنْجَاءُ)
2. Washing the hands before entering them into the vessel
3. Pronouncing the name of God when sitting down for ablution
4. Rinsing the mouth
5. Drawing water into the nose
6. Moving the ring so that the water reaches what is beneath it
7. Combing the water through the beard
8. Wetting the eyes with water
9. Giving the right limbs precedence over the left
10. Wiping the ears — their inner and outer parts — with water
11. The second and third washings of the face, each a practice, while the first is the obligation
12. The siwak (السِّوَاك)

We say that the greater purity (اَلطَّهَارَةُ الْكُبْرَى), which is the washing of the whole body, is likewise divided into seven obligations and twelve practices. The obligations are:

1. The washing from janabah (الْجَنَابَة)
2. The washing from menstruation
3. The washing of the unbeliever when he enters Islam
4. The washing of one who has fallen unconscious when he recovers
5. The washing from the blood of nifas (النِّفَاس)
6. The washing after immersion in impurity
7. The washing of the dead, which is an obligation upon the living until one of them performs it

The practices are:

1. The washing of Friday
2. The washing for the festival of al-Fitr
3. The washing for the festival of al-Adha
4. The washing for ihram
5. The washing for entering the Haram
6. The washing for entering the Kabah
7. The washing for entering Madinah
8. The washing on the day of Arafah
9. The washing on three nights of the month of Ramadan, the night of the nineteenth
10. The night of the twenty-first
11. The night of the twenty-third
12. The washing after washing the dead

Our lord Amir al-Muminin Ali ibn Abi Talib (ع) said in his four hundred maxims of conduct:

> تَنَظَّفُوا بِالْمَاءِ مِنَ الرِّيحِ الْمُنْتِنَةِ

Cleanse yourselves with water from the foul odor.

And he said therein:

> إذا أراد أحدكم الخلاء فليقل بسم الله اللهم أمط عني الأذى وأعذني من الشيطان الرجيم الحمد لله الذي أطعمنيه في عافية وأخرج مني أذاه في عافية

When any of you intends to go to the privy, let him say: "In the name of God. O God, remove the filth from me and protect me from the accursed devil. Praise be to God, who fed me in good health and expelled its harm from me in good health."

> إِذَا نَظَرَ أَحَدُكُمْ إِلَىٰ حَدَثِهِ بَعْدَ فَرَاغِهِ فَلْيَقُلِ اللَّهُمَّ ارْزُقْنِي الْحَلَالَ وَجَنِّبْنِي الْحَرَامَ فَاِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّىٰ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ قَالَ مَا مِنْ عَبْدٍ إِلَّا وَقَدْ وَكَّلَ اللَّهُ بِهِ مَلَكًا يَلْوِي عُنُقَهُ إِذَا أَحْدَثَ حَتَّىٰ يَنْظُرَ إِلَيْهِ وَيَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ يَسْأَلَ اللَّهَ الْحَلَالَ فَاِنَّ الْمَلَكَ يَقُولُ يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ هَٰذَا مَا حَرَصْتَ عَلَيْهِ فَانْظُرْ مِنْ أَيْنَ أَخَذْتَهُ وَإِلَىٰ مَا صَارَ

When one of you looks at what has passed from him after he finishes, let him say: O God, grant me the lawful and keep me from the unlawful. For the Messenger of God said: There is no servant but that God has appointed over him an angel who turns his neck when he relieves himself, so that he looks at it. It is fitting for him to ask God for the lawful, for the angel says: O son of Adam, this is the thing you were so eager for — consider where you took it from and what it has come to.

He also said in that same context:

> إِذَا خَالَطَ النَّوْمُ الْقَلْبَ وَجَبَ الْوُضُوءُ

When sleep mingles with the heart, ablution becomes obligatory.

chapters.chapter_key: major impurity and the cleanliness of things
chapters.before_md:
### Mentioning the Ghusl from Janabah

I take the questions and answers that follow from the book of questions and answers mentioned earlier, which one of its compilers arranged according to the chapters of the book *Daaim al-Islam*.

Question: What do you say, O best of those for whom our tongues fall short in praise and gratitude, concerning what has come in certain books of the Shariah: that when a man fears the cold and a ghusl is due upon him, he performs tayammum and prays, and then, when he is able to use water, he washes and repeats the prayer? Does this ruling apply equally to the resident and the traveler, or not?

Answer: If he fears that the water will harm him — whether he is a resident or a traveler — he performs tayammum and prays, and nothing further is required of him.

Question: What do you say, O one to whose excellence the far and the near both bear witness, concerning the ghusl from janabah (جَنَابَة), since marital relations are a likeness of imparting and receiving? Explain, then, the likeness of the washing and what the one who washes is obliged to call to mind while washing, for the exposition of this in the books of the guiding Dawah is very long.

Answer: The washing is a likeness of the removal of doubt, and doubt arises only at the moment of imparting and receiving.

Question: What do you say, O one whom God Most High has made a rope extended from heaven to this world for the people of the earth who remember God while sitting and while standing, concerning what has come in the Shariah: that one who has fallen unconscious, when he revives after some days and does not know whether he may have become in a state of janabah, must perform the ghusl? O our master, what is the measure of this if he sees no trace of semen?

Answer: If he does not know his own condition, the ghusl becomes obligatory upon him once doubt has entered him concerning it.

Question: What does our master say — may God inspire him with the welfare of the Dawah — concerning a weak man who has been overtaken by janabah and who fears the cold if he washes, when the time of prayer has come? May he perform tayammum as the sick man does, or not?

Answer: If he fears the water, he performs tayammum and prays, and he does not repeat the prayer.

Question: What does our master say — may God perpetuate his support — concerning a man who wakes from sleep and sees on his garment the trace of semen, wet or dry, though he did not see in his sleep that he had emitted? Is the ghusl obligatory upon him or not?

Answer: The ghusl is obligatory upon him.

Question: What do you say, O fulfiller of the needs of those who ask, concerning what is mentioned in the Shariah: that it is disliked for the one in janabah and for the menstruating woman to remove from themselves any hair or nail, and that the woman in post-natal bleeding is in the same state as the menstruating woman? O our master, is this permitted to them despite the dislike, or is it not permitted at all?

Answer: To leave it is better, until such a one is purified.

Question: What do you say, O one whom I approached from where I came — out of nothing but pure love — concerning the one in janabah and the menstruating woman who read supplications or other books in which there is something of the Quran, whether the reader recognizes it or does not? How is such a one to act — reading it or leaving it — when it has come in the radiant Shariah that the two do not recite the Quran and do not touch it? And may the one in janabah and the menstruating woman recite the declaration of God's oneness, the magnification, the praise, and the glorification, all of which are in the Quran? And may such a one recite the *basmalah* (اَلْبَسْمَلَة), when it has been said that it is a verse of the Quran?

Answer: Neither the menstruating woman nor the one in janabah may recite the Quran, nor any part of it in a supplication or in books, deliberately; and neither may recite the *basmalah* with the intention of reciting the Quran.

In the book *Mukhtasar al-Musannaf* it is said that whoever forgets the ablution until he has performed the ghusl performs the ablution, and there is nothing against him. It is also said there: when a man has performed the ablution and then begins the ghusl, and a minor impurity occurs before he has completed his washing, he continues with the ghusl and performs the ablution after it for the prayer.

Among the answers of certain summoners of Yemen to certain dignitaries of the Indian lands (رض): if one in janabah and a deceased person are brought together and there is not found of water except what suffices for one of them, the one in janabah performs the ghusl and tayammum is performed for the deceased.

The author of *al-Risala al-Maknuna* said: God has imposed the ghusl from janabah, for He said — exalted be He who speaks:

> وَإِن كُنتُمْ جُنُبًۭا فَٱطَّهَّرُوا۟
>
> "And if you are in a state of major impurity, then purify yourselves."

And the Prophet said:

> تَحْتَ كُلِّ شَعْرٍ جَنَابَةٌ فَبُلُّوا الشَّعْرَ وَاَنْقُوا الْبَشَرَ
>
> "Beneath every hair there is major impurity, so wet the hair and cleanse the skin."

Then he said: whoever does not do that is junub, and al-junub is the one far from a thing. It is said, "he is a stranger to me" — that is, far from my lineage. And the obedience of the one in janabah is void and false.

The Commander of the Faithful, our master Ali ibn Abi Talib (ع), said in his Four Hundred Manners:

> لَا يَنَامُ الْمُسْلِمُ وَهُوَ جُنُبٌ وَلَا يَنَامُ اِلَّا وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ طَهُورٍ فَاِنْ لَمْ يَجِدِ الْمَاءَ فَلْيَتَيَمَّمْ بِالصَّعِيدِ فَاِنَّ رُوحَ الْمُؤْمِنِ تَرْتَفِعُ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فَيَقْبَلُهَا وَيُبَارِكُ عَلَيْهَا فَاِنْ كَانَ قَدْ حَضَرَ أَجَلُهَا جَعَلَهَا فِي أَحْسَنِ صُورَةٍ وَاِنْ لَمْ يَحْضُرْ أَجَلُهَا بَعَثَ بِهَا مَعَ أُمَنَاءِهِ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ فَرَدُّوهَا إِلَىٰ جَسَدِهِ

### Mentioning the Purity of Bodies, Garments, Ground, Carpets, and What Belongs to That

I take these also from the book of question and answer mentioned earlier, arranged according to the chapters of *Daaim al-Islam*.

**Question:** What do you say, O best of those who have commanded us to endure with patience the decree of God and His judgment, concerning vomit? Does it render impure what it falls upon, as blood and pus and the other impurities do, or not?

**Answer:** Vomit does not render impure what it falls upon, though it is better that the place be washed.

**Question:** What do you say, O one whom God Most High has made a provision for the traveler who wishes to arrive at God Most High, concerning ground on which children urinate and relieve themselves, which then dries so that the smell of the impurity and its substance are gone from it? Is prayer upon it permissible without a mat, and is tayammum from it permissible, or not?

**Answer:** If the substance of the impurity has gone, its ruling is the ruling of pure ground, provided it is not ground set aside as a privy for need.

**Question:** What do you say, O one whom God Most High has made a measure by which the corrupt is tested against the pure in the religion of God, concerning what has come in the Shariah: that when impurity strikes the ground and water then runs over it and it dries, and the smell of the impurity and its substance are gone from it, prayer upon it and tayammum from it are permitted? And it has also come that there is no harm in praying in the dry places among the resting grounds of camels and the folds of sheep. O our master, what is the difference between this and that?

**Answer:** The sun and the light purify it. So when the substance of the impurity and its smell have gone from it, prayer upon it and tayammum from it are permitted.

**Question:** What does our master say, may God make lasting the throne of his governance, concerning the meaning of the words of the Commander of the Faithful:

> مَنْ مَسَّ جَسَدَ مَيِّتٍ بَعْدَ أَنْ يَبْرُدَ لَزِمَهُ الْغُسْلُ
>
> "Whoever touches the body of a dead man after it has grown cold must perform the ghusl."

What is the meaning of his words, "after it has grown cold"?

**Answer:** Its meaning is: after it has become impure. So when it touches the living with its moisture, he becomes impure, and this is the meaning of the ghusl becoming binding — that it be decreed upon him. And the washing performed by the one who washes the corpse is from the Sunnah.

**Question:** Concerning a thing that a man wishes to purify but is not able to rub or to wring out three times — such as a fur, a mat, a rug, the quilts used in the mosque, and bedding — what is the manner of purifying it?

**Answer:** For a thing that a man wishes to purify but is not able to rub or to wring out three times, he passes his hand over it until the impurity and its smell are gone, then lifts it from the water and leaves it until what is in it has dripped out, then repeats this three times. As for what is other than this, he treads it with his feet in the manner described, then takes it out of the water and presses upon it until the water has come out of it, then repeats this three times.

**Question:** Concerning a woman's milk that falls upon the garment of another, is it pure or not?

**Answer:** From the Walid Izz al-Din Maad ibn Abdullah ibn Ali: the milk of a nursing woman, if she is a Muslim, is pure, both for her and for others. And I say that this is an established position, since her milk is like her saliva, and the saliva of every Muslim is pure and does not render impure what it touches.

**Question:** Concerning a man who shaves his head, and something of his hair falls while it is wet upon his garment or upon his body: does that hair render impure what it touches or not?

**Answer:** If that is a small amount, then a small amount of impurity has been excused.

**Question:** Concerning the animals that feed upon filth — of cattle and camels and sheep — and the milk and clarified butter of these, and the white of the eggs of hens, when they fall upon the garments of those praying or upon their bodies: does this render them impure or not?

**Answer:** That follows what was mentioned in the first case: a small amount of it is excused.

**Question:** Concerning the traveler and the sick man, whose garments are touched by impurity and who are not able to cleanse them, is the prayer complete for them with tayammum, or must it be made up afterward?

**Answer:** The prayer is not complete except with a pure garment. Tayammum has been mentioned for ritual impurity, and it has not been mentioned for the impurity of garments. As for the sick man, he instructs someone to wash his garments for him.

**Question:** The polytheist worships idols and knows neither the lawful nor the forbidden, and he weaves the cloth, and after that he bleaches it, and after that he sews it. Is his work pure, and is prayer in it permitted or not? For God Most High has said:

> إِنَّمَا ٱلْمُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌۭ
>
> "The polytheists are nothing but impurity."

**Answer:** All such garments are pure until he wears them; and if he has worn them, then they are impure, or if impurity has appeared in them. As he said in the book *al-Daaim*:

> ورخصوا الأئمة صلوات الله عليهم في الصلاة في الثياب التي يعملها المشركين ما لم يلبسوها أو تظهر فيها النجاسة

He said also: the same applies to a dyed garment when the dyer is a polytheist — it remains pure until he has worn it; once he has worn it, it is impure.

**Question:** What does our master say, may God perpetuate his support, concerning the bleaching that polytheists perform on whatever they bleach — does it carry purity or not? Be so good as to make this clear.

**Answer:** I say — trusting in God's granting of success and drawing support from the blessings of His friends — that there is no path to the purity of polytheists' garments except those they have made before wearing them. As for what they have bleached and washed with soap, its purity is not allowed except by washing. Perhaps those who heard the saying about this did not grasp the root of the question in it.

**Question:** What does our master say, may God perpetuate his support, concerning the garments of polytheists التي they have made but have not worn, which they sprinkle with impure water at the time of the weaving and the spinning, after which the water dries and the garments are sold, and they have neither worn them nor washed them with soap? Is prayer in them permitted or not?

**Answer:** There is no harm in praying in them, and the radiant Shariah has permitted them.

**Question:** What do you say, O one whose people of response have come to take pride in the praiseworthy account of his conduct, concerning the wide, long garment and the bedding of which one part is pure and another part impure? Is prayer performed upon the part of it that is pure? For the common people say that if the garment is of such a size that when one end of it is moved the other end does not move, prayer is permitted upon the part of it that is pure.

**Answer:** One does not pray upon it, and prayer upon it is not permitted.

In the book *Mukhtasar al-Musannaf* it is said that prayer in the garments of children who guard themselves against impurity is permitted so long as no impurity is known in them, and dispensation has been given for a slight sprinkling. It is said there also: as for the houses out in the open country, praying in them has not been forbidden, though it is not recommended.

I turn now to the book of question and answer whose questions are from the most excellent Sheikh Yusuf ibn Ismail ibn Ibrahim al-Samti al-Hindi and whose answers are from our master Idris ibn al-Hasan.

**Question:** Is prayer permitted upon stone and upon plaster? Favor us with a sufficient and clear answer.

**Answer:** The Prophet said:

> جُعِلَتْ لِي الْأَرْضُ مَسْجِدًا وَطَهُورًا
>
> "The earth has been made for me a place of prostration and a means of purification."

Anything of the ground from which tayammum is not permitted may not be prayed upon.

**Question:** What do you say about sweeping houses? Most people in India hold that houses must not be swept at night at all, and they treat it as a religious scruple; they likewise hold that shops and stalls are not to be swept at night. How does this stand — may God make us your ransom?

**Answer:** This view is not reliable, and there is no blame on one who does it.

In *Tawil al-Shariah* it is recorded that the Prophet said:

> إِذَا وَلَغَ الْكَلْبُ فِي إِنَاءِ أَحَدِكُمْ فَلْيَغْسِلْهُ سَبْعَ مَرَّاتٍ إِحْدَاهُنَّ بِالتُّرَابِ
>
> "When a dog laps from the vessel of one of you, let him wash it seven times, one of them with earth."

*Mukhtasar al-Musannaf* states: when a vessel becomes impure from a dog's lapping, it is washed seven times, the first of them with earth, and the pig is treated the same way. It is also stated there: if impurity falls into one of two vessels and it is not known which of them it is, neither vessel is to be approached; one performs tayammum and prays.

The Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (ع), said in his Four Hundred Manners:

> أَخْذُ الشَّارِبِ مِنَ النَّظَافَةِ وَهُوَ مِنَ السُّنَّةِ
>
> "Trimming the mustache is part of cleanliness, and it is of the Sunnah."

> غَسْلُ الرَّأْسِ بِالْحِطْمِيِّ يُذْهِبُ بِالدَّرَنِ وَهُوَ مِنَ السُّنَّةِ وَيَنْفِي الْأَقْذَارَ
>
> "Washing the head with mallow takes away grime, and it is of the Sunnah, and it drives off filth."

> النُّورَةُ مَشَدَّةٌ لِلْبَدَنِ وَطَهُورٌ لِلْجَسَدِ
>
> "The depilatory paste strengthens the body and is a purification for the flesh."

> تَقْلِيمُ الْأَظَافِرِ يَمْنَعُ الدَّاءَ الْأَعْظَمَ وَيَجْلِبُ الرِّزْقَ وَيَدُرُّهُ
>
> "Trimming the nails wards off the greatest disease, and draws sustenance and makes it flow."

> نَتْفُ الْآبَاطِ يَنْفِي الرَّائِحَةَ الْمُنْكَرَةَ وَهُوَ طَهُورٌ وَهُوَ مِنَ السُّنَّةِ
>
> "Plucking the armpits removes the offensive odor; it is a purification, and it is of the Sunnah."

> غُسْلُ الْأَعْيَادِ طَهُورٌ لِمَنْ طَلَبَ الْحَوَائِجَ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَأتِّبَاعُ السُّنَّةِ
>
> "Bathing on the feast days is a purification for whoever presents his needs before God, mighty and majestic, and a following of the Sunnah."

> غَسْلُ الثِّيَابِ يُذْهِبُ بِالْهَمِّ وَيَكْبِتُ الْعَدُوَّ وَهُوَ طَهُورٌ لِلصَّلَاةِ
>
> "Washing the garments takes away anxiety and subdues the enemy, and it is a purification for the prayer."

> لَا تَنْتِفُوا الشَّنَبَ فَاِنَّهُ نُورٍ لِلْمُسْلِمِ
>
> "Do not pluck out the mustache, for it is a light for the Muslim."

> مَنْ شَابَ فِي رَأْسِهِ شَيْبَةٌ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ كَانَتْ لَهُ نُورًا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
>
> "Whoever grows a white hair upon his head while in Islam, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection."

> ولا يتغوّطنّ أحدكم على الحجة ولا يبل في سطح الهواء ولا في ماء راكد فمن فعل فأصابه شيء فلا يلومنّ الا نفسه فان للماء أهلاً وللهواء أهلاً فإذا بال أحدكم فلا يطمحنّ ببوله ولا يستقبل به الربح
>
> "Let none of you relieve himself on the road, nor urinate into the open air or into standing water. Whoever does so and something befalls him, let him blame none but himself — for the water has its folk, and the air has its folk. And when one of you urinates, let him not make his urine splash, and let him not face the wind with it."

> ولا ينا منّ أحدكم على الحجة ولا على وجهه فمن رأيتموه نام على وجهه فانبهوه
>
> "And let none of you sleep on the road, nor upon his face. Whoever you see sleeping upon his face, wake him."

> تَنَظَّفُوا بِالْمَاءِ مِنَ الرِّيحِ الْمُنْتِنَةِ وَتَعَاهَدُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ فَاِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى يُبْغِضُ الْعَبْدَ الْقَاذُورَةَ الَّذِي یَتَأَذَّى بِهِ مَنْ جَلَسَ إِلَيْهِ
>
> "Cleanse yourselves of foul odor with water, and take care of your cleanliness, for God Most High hates the filthy servant who offends those who sit near him."

> تَنَزَّهُوا عَنْ قُرْبِ الْكِلَابِ فَمَنْ أَصَابَهُ كَلْبٌ جَافٌّ فَلْيَنْضَحْ ثَوْبَهُ بِالْمَاءِ وَاِنْ كَانَ الْكَلْبُ رَطِبًا فَلْيَغْسِلْهُ
>
> "Keep yourselves away from dogs. Whoever is touched by a dry dog should sprinkle his garment with water; if the dog was wet, he must wash it."

> اُحِبُّ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ أَنْ يَطَّلِّيَ فِي كُلِّ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا مَرَّةً بِنُورَةٍ
>
> "I love for the believer that he anoint himself once every fifteen days with the depilatory paste."

What follows I take from a book of questions and answers: the questions come from the most excellent Sheikh Shimon ibn Muhammad Ghori al-Hindi (رض), and the answers are from our master Badr al-Din, our master Hasan ibn Idris.

Question: What do you say, O one by whom our souls have life, concerning a man who lets the hair of his head grow long and neither combs nor parts it each day? Does his prayer suffer any defect, or not? And how often ought he to comb and part it?

Answer: If he parts it into two halves, there is no defect upon him; yet it is not fitting that he leave it without a parting. If he does so deliberately, in defiance of the ruling, his prayer is void.

Question: What do you say concerning the meaning of the words of Ali (ع):

> مَنْ لَا يُطَهِّرُهُ الْبَحْرُ فَلَا طَهَّرَهُ اللهُ
>
> "Whomever the sea does not purify, may God not purify him."

Answer: Water purifies and is not itself purified. So likewise is the knowledge of the Imam: whomever it does not purify, God does not purify him.

chapters.chapter_key: what the worshipper wears and stands upon
chapters.before_md:
I turn now to the dress of the worshipper and what he prostrates upon.

In the book of questions and answers mentioned at the outset — the one whose arranger organized it according to the chapters of the book دَعَائِمُ الْإِسْلَامِ (Pillars of Islam) — I find the following exchanges.

Question: What is your ruling on the prayer mat, the rug, and other cloths on which the qibla or another image is depicted, in such a way that it does not occupy the worshipper when he looks at it? Is prayer upon such items permitted, whether the image falls in the place of prostration or elsewhere?

Answer: If it is of a kind that occupies the worshipper when he looks at it, prayer is not permitted. If it does not occupy him, prayer is permitted — except in the case of images, toward which he does not pray.

Question: What is your ruling on a man who prays in a garment dyed with safflower that is not deeply red? Is his prayer permitted? And what of a woman who prays in pure silk, or in a garment of a very deep red, whether dyed with safflower or not? Is her prayer permitted?

Answer: This belongs to the domain of etiquette. If anyone wears such a garment, it does not invalidate the prayer performed in it, whether the wearer is a man or a woman — except for pure silk, which is disliked for men.

Question: What is your ruling on what has come in the books of the Sharia — that if any part of a woman's عورة ('awra) becomes exposed during prayer her prayer is spoiled, whether she knew of it or not? The women of the people of the dawa in India do not customarily wear the long shift and the head-veil, and their legs are uncovered during prayer once or twice. How then does their prayer stand?

Answer: Covering is indispensable, for the whole of a woman is عورة. If any part of her awra is exposed, prayer is not permitted to her, whether she knew this ruling or was ignorant of it. This is its meaning.

Question: Concerning the man wading through water, the man in fear, and the traveler pressing hard upon his journey — men who carry weaponry that bars them from prayer, such as the feathering of arrows, leather straps, the trimmings of daggers, and garments of pure silk — is their prayer complete without repetition, or not?

Answer: Prayer is valid only in pure garments. Whatever is impure, the worshipper strips from himself.

Question: What is your ruling on a man who prays while carrying weights of gold and silver upon him, wrought or unwrought, tucked into his waistband? Is his prayer established or not?

Answer: His prayer is complete and established.

Question: The abridgment of the Musannaf states that there is no harm in praying upon a rug bearing figures, so long as they are not in the place of prostration and do not divert him from the prayer. Is prayer upon such a rug permitted? And likewise, if garments bearing figures are worn, is prayer in them permitted?

Answer: As for the rug and the garment bearing figures, prayer is not permitted when they are seen. When they are not seen, prayer in them and upon them is permitted.

Question: If the worshipper prays upon stone, upon unbaked brick, or upon the like of these, is prayer upon them permitted or not?

Answer: Obligatory prayer upon them is not permitted; only the supererogatory and the sunna prayer.

Question: What is your ruling on a man who applies henna to his hand or foot for adornment and not for any benefit? Is that permitted?

Answer: It is not fitting that men use henna for adornment. Women are commanded to use it. For men, to leave it aside without cause is better, though no sin falls upon one who does it.

From another place: prayer is permitted in the garments of the children of Muslims and the slaves of Muslims, so long as no impurity appears in them and none is seen, when they themselves do not pray. Whoever prays, then finishes his prayer, and then sees that his garment was impure — if he knew of it beforehand, his prayer is void and he repeats it, whether its time has passed or not. A man is not to pray bareheaded, without turban and without mantle; but if he finds neither, he prays. Whoever prays leaving upon his shoulders only a small kerchief — that is, his handcloth — while he has another garment available, his prayer is not permitted; but if he finds nothing else, his prayer in it is permitted.

The book of the abridgment of the Musannaf states: if a man prays with his 'awra (عَوْرَة) uncovered and does not know of it until he has finished the prayer, he must repeat it once he comes to know. And if a free woman or a slave woman prays with her awra uncovered — whether she knew of it or not — her prayer is spoiled.

Our master Jafar ibn Mansur al-Yaman, may God exalt his sanctity, says in the book of the obligations and the limits of religion: it is lawful for a man to uncover his head openly, to go out among the congregation, and to pray with his head uncovered. If a man prays with something in his mouth — such as a gemstone, a dirham, or the like — and it does not prevent him from forming the letters properly, his prayer is complete. If he is holding something in his hand and it does not prevent him from fulfilling the limits of his prayer, there is no harm upon him; yet to be free of it is better for him.

From the same source: whoever has nothing but an impure garment, can obtain no other, and has no water with which to purify it, prays in it and repeats the prayer when he finds another garment or water to purify it. If he has two garments, one of them impure, but does not know which one, it is incumbent upon him to pray that prayer in each of them, intending by it the performance of the obligation. There is no harm in praying upon a rug bearing figures, so long as they are not in the place of prostration and do not divert him from the prayer. As for plaster and the like, over which carrion is burned and with which the mosque and the house are plastered, there is no harm in prostrating upon it, for the fire has purified it.

In the book of the interpretation of the Daaim, upon the saying:

> وَلَا بَأْسَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ فِي الْقَمِيصِ الْوَاحِدِ الْكَثِيفِ إِذَا أَزَرَّهُ

There is no harm in praying in a single thick shirt if he belts it — meaning the worshipper. The sense of this is that, when he bows, his private part should not appear from its edge.

From the same, upon the saying:

> مَثَلُ جَنَاحَيِ الْخُطَّافِ

Like the two wings of the swallow. This means a garment that he wraps over his back and whose two ends he brings back upon his shoulders, when he finds nothing other than that.

From the same, upon the saying:

> نَهَىٰ عَنِ اشْتِمَالِ الصَّمَّاءِ

He forbade the wrapping called اِشْتِمَالُ الصَّمَّاءِ. That is when a man wraps himself in a single garment, setting its middle upon his head or upon his shoulders, drawing one end with his left hand against his body, and turning the end on his right toward his left and behind him, gathering it with his right hand, so that he becomes as though sewn into it with both his hands beneath it. If he prays in this condition, he cannot perform the prayer properly: he cannot set his palms upon the ground as required, he cannot bow or prostrate, and he cannot manage the raising of his hands. Such a prayer is therefore incomplete and does not suffice him.

The book of the abridgment of the Musannaf states: as for the slave woman, the woman under a contract of manumission, the woman freed at her master's death, and the girl who has not yet reached menstruation, there is no harm in their praying without a head covering. Whichever of them is set free while she does not know of it must repeat every prayer she prayed after her freedom without a head covering.

The book of questions and answers — whose questions come from the most venerable Shaykh Yusuf ibn Ismail ibn Ibrahim al-Samati al-Hindi and whose answers come from our master Idris ibn al-Hasan, may God exalt his sanctity — contains the following. Question: Is prayer permitted upon stones and plaster? Favor us with a clear and sufficient answer. Answer: The Prophet said:

> جُعِلَتْ لِي الْأَرْضُ مَسْجِدًا وَطَهُورًا

The earth has been made for me a place of prostration and a means of purification.

And everything of the earth with which dry ablution is not permitted — prayer upon it is not permitted.

The book of questions on matters of the Sharia and their answers — containing one hundred and three questions, put by certain eminent shaykhs of India and answered by certain callers from Yemen, may God sanctify their souls — records the following.

**The seventeenth question:** Concerning a free woman who prays with a net upon her head — does the net serve her in place of a mantle, or not? **Answer:** It is not recorded that prayer in a shift and head-veil suffices unless both are thick; and the net does not cover.

**The fourth question:** Concerning camels, cattle, and sheep that feed upon filth — when their milk and their clarified butter, or the egg whites of hens, reach the garments or bodies of those praying, do they render them impure or not? **Answer:** A small amount of it is permitted.

It is said in the book of the interpretation of the Sharia: there is no prayer except upon the earth or upon what grows from it, such as green plants. And it is said therein: the Prophet said:

> حُبِّبَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ دُنْيَاكُمْ ثَلَاثَةٌ النِّسَاءُ وَالطِّيبُ وَجُعِلَتْ قُرَّةُ عَيْنِي فِي الصَّلَاةِ

Three things of your world have been made beloved to me: women and perfume, and the delight of my eye has been placed in prayer.

And it is said therein: the Prophet (ع) said:

> كُلُّ صَلَاةٍ لَا يُقْرَأُ فِيهَا بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ فَهِيَ خِدَاجٌ غَيْرُ تَامَّةٍ

Every prayer in which the Opening of the Book is not recited is defective and incomplete.

And it is said therein:

> لَا صَلَاةَ فِي أَعْطَانِ الْإِبِلِ وَلَا بَأْسَ بِالصَّلَاةِ فِي مَرَابِضِ الْغَنَمِ بَعْدَ أَنْ تُكْنَسَ وَتُرَشَّ

Prayer is not valid in the resting places of camels. There is, however, no harm in praying in the folds of sheep once they have been swept and sprinkled with water.

Our master the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (ع), said in his four hundred counsels of etiquette:

> لَا يَقُومَنَّ أَحَدُكُمْ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ اِلَّا وَعَلَيْهِ ثَوْبٌ نَظِيفٌ

Let none of you stand before God, the Mighty and Exalted, except in a clean garment.

And he said therein:

> لا يصلي الرجل في قميص متوشحاً فأنه فعل قوم لوط

A man is not to pray in a shirt draped loosely across him, for that is the practice of the people of Lot.

And he said therein:

> لَا تَجُوزُ الصَّلَاةُ فِي ثَوْبٍ يُعَسْطِلُ فِيهِ عَلَى عُنُقِهِ وَفِي الْقَمِيِّصِ الصَّفِيقِ يَرُدُّهُ عَلَيْهِ

Prayer is not permitted in a garment that hangs slack about his neck, nor in a close-woven shirt unless he draws it over himself.

And he said therein:

> لَا يَسْجُدُ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى صُورَةٍ وَلَا عَلَى بِسَاطٍ هِيَ فِيهِ

A man must not prostrate upon an image, nor upon a rug that contains one.

And he said therein:

> وَلَا يَعْقِدُ الرَّجُلُ الدِّرْهَمَ الَّذِي فِيهِ الصُّورَةُ فِي ثَوْبِهِ وَهُوَ يُصَلِّي وَتَجُوزُ أَنْ تَكُونَ الدَّرَاهِمُ فِي هِمْيَانٍ أَوْ ثَوْبٍ إِذَا كَانَ طَاهِرًا وَلَا يَسْجُدُ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى كُدْسِ الْحِنْطَةِ وَلَا عَلَى شَعِيرٍ وَلَا عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِمَّا يُؤْكَلُ وَلَا عَلَى الْخُبْزِ

A man must not knot a dirham bearing an image into his garment while praying. It is, however, permitted for coins to be carried in a money belt or in a cloth, provided it is clean. He must not prostrate upon a heap of wheat, barley, anything edible, or bread.

### On the Friday Prayer

I turn now to the Friday prayer, and I set down first what I find in the book of questions and answers mentioned at the outset — which one of its arrangers ordered according to the chapters of *Daaim al-Islam*.

The question: What do you say concerning what has come in the Book of Purity — that if three miles or more separate two congregational mosques, Friday prayer is established in each of them, whether they stand in one city or two; but if the distance between them in a single city falls short of that, Friday prayer is established in only one of them? Our master, if the distance is less than three miles and the two mosques belong to two separate cities, is Friday prayer established in both of them or not?

The answer: Friday prayer is not established in both when the distance between them is less than three miles, whether they belong to one city or to two.

The question concerns the words of our master al-Muayyad in the Friday sermon:

> فَمَنْ تَرَكَهَا مُتَعَمِّداً أَوْ مُسْتَخِفّاً بِحَقِّهَا مِنْ غَيْرِ عُذْرٍ لَهُ مَعَ إِمَامٍ عَدْلٍ أَوْ جَائِرٍ فَلَا تَجْمَعِ اللهُ شَمْلَهُ

Whoever abandons it deliberately, or makes light of its due, without excuse — whether under a just imam or an unjust one — may God not gather his affairs together; to the end of the passage.

The answer: It is not permissible to pray behind the people of injustice except for the sake of dissimulation, as has come in the Shariah from Mawlana al-Baqir Muhammad ibn Ali (ع), who said:

Do not count the prayer behind a الناصب or a الحروري as valid. Treat such a person as one of the pillars of المسجد and recite for yourself, as though you were praying alone.

> لَا تَعْتَدَّ بِالصَّلَاةِ خَلْفَ النَّاصِبِ وَلَا الْحَرُورِيِّ وَاجْعَلْهُ سَارِيَةً مِنْ سَوَارِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَاقْرَأْ لِنَفْسِكَ كَأَنَّكَ وَحْدَكَ

The commentary on the reports records that al-Husayn ibn Ali (ع) put the governor of Muawiya forward to lead the prayer over his brother al-Hasan ibn Ali (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), and said:

> لَوْلَا السُّنَّةُ لَمَا قَدَّمْتُكَ

Were it not for the practice, I would not have put you forward.

By that, he meant the practice of the People of the House (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) in dissimulation — as one of the Imams (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) said:

> التَّقِيَّةُ دِينِي وَدِينُ آبَائِي

Dissimulation is my religion and the religion of my fathers.

As for what is meant by "the unjust" in his words, it refers to whoever has been set up among the summoners and from whom injustice and transgression have appeared: it is obligatory to pray behind him, and it is incumbent upon the people, when they observe this in him, to bring the matter before the holder of authority and to await his response. This is the meaning of his saying:

> أَيُّهَا الصَّالِحُونَ فَتَحَقَّقُوا ذَلِكَ وَلَا تَرْتَابُوا بَعْدَ الْيَقِينِ فَقَدِ اعْتَصَمْتُمْ بِجَبَلِ اللَّهِ الْمَتِينِ

O righteous ones, verify this and do not fall into doubt after certainty, for you have taken firm hold of the strong mountain of God.

He says in the book *Mukhtasar al-Musannaf*: The Friday prayer behind the Imam of the Muslims is more excellent than the prayer behind his deputies. If the Imam is delayed because he is occupied with some of the interests of the Muslims, and his deputies pray in his stead in mosques that are near one another, then the prayer in his own mosque — the one in which it has been his custom to pray — is more fitting than in any other.

He says in it: The call to prayer that obliges the one upon whom the Friday duty rests to leave off buying and selling is the call given in the presence of the preacher when he sits in the place from which he delivers the sermon. If two of those obliged to the Friday prayer transact a sale at the time when it is forbidden, their sale is not annulled. Whoever grows thirsty while the Imam is on the pulpit may drink.

He says in it: If the Imam delivers the sermon on Friday and his state of purity is broken, he descends and performs the ablution; then if he wishes he repeats the sermon, and if he wishes he prays — all of this suffices him. If he delivers the sermon seated because of an ailment, that suffices him. It is disliked for him to omit the sitting between the two sermons, but if he has done so, repetition is not obligatory upon him.

If the Imam delivers the sermon on Friday and then some matter overtakes the people and they go off to it, and only one man remains with him, then he prays four cycles. If he has delivered the sermon to the people on Friday and prayed one cycle with them and then they all departed and he remained alone, he prays the Friday prayer as two cycles. If he has opened the prayer and they departed before he bowed, he begins afresh the noon prayer of four cycles. If the Imam prays the Friday prayer with the people, and when he has finished the second cycle he rises to stand and then remembers, it is upon him to sit, to make the testimony, to give the greeting of peace, and to perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness.

And from it: Whoever among the people of Friday sleeps while waiting for the Friday prayer, and the prayer is established and purification is not possible for him, performs the dry ablution and prays with the Imam, then repeats it as four.

He says in the book of reports: And he leans upon his sword; if he does not find a sword, then upon a staff.

He says in the book *Tawil al-Shariah*: The sermon is before the prayer, and the prayer after the sermon is two cycles. He divides the sermon into two portions with a sitting that separates them. The raising of the voice in its recitation distinguishes it from the noon prayer on the remaining days, and the noon prayer is at seven hours. He said: The call to stand for prayer comes after the sermon.

He says in it: The practice of the respondents in the assembly of the summoner is like the practice of the congregation on Friday, or the congregation behind the Imam. When the preacher on Friday ascends the pulpit and faces the people, silence becomes obligatory, such that it is not permissible for anyone to speak or to occupy himself with anything other than listening to him and giving ear to him.

He says in it: It is not permissible for him to give suck unless his summoner has appointed him to the suckling and chosen him for it. When the Imam recites, listening becomes obligatory and nothing else, and it is not permissible to turn away from him. Likewise, it is not permissible for the respondent to press proposals upon the summoner or to demand from him the various branches of knowledge, for he knows better how to raise his children.

Our master Zayd ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl said in his *Hidden Epistle*: The Friday prayer points to Muhammad (ع), who is the gate of the Garden, and he has two summonses — an outward summons to the outward face of his Shariah and an inward summons to the interpretation of his law. Then he said: Because the prayer on the remaining days was four cycles, on Friday it became two, and the sermon was made a substitute for the two cycles. It is praise, admonition, supplication, and exposition from the Lord of exposition, and it is never without warning. The sitting during the sermon is the separation between the upper light and the lower light; the Qaim (ع) rises with the two lights. Then he said: The preacher is not to deliver the sermon upon the call to prayer that has already been given, until the muezzin who stands before the seat gives the call after the Imam has ascended the pulpit. Then he said: The call is given only in the congregational mosque, as an announcement. Then he said: Whoever gives the call on that day in one of the mosques other than the congregational mosque has erred, and if he did it deliberately he is punished and commanded to perform the washing of Friday. Then he said:

> فَاعْرِفْ فَضْلَ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ حَتَّىٰ يَجْمَعَ اللَّهُ شَمْلَكَ بِيَوْمِ السَّبْتِ فَتَسْتَرِيحَ وَتَسْبُتَ وَلَا تَشْقَىٰ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَىٰ

Know the excellence of the day of Friday, so that God may gather your affairs together on the day of the Sabbath and you may rest and repose, spared from wretchedness — if God the Exalted wills.

Mawlana Amir al-Muminin Ali ibn Abi Talib (ع) said in his Four Hundred Points of Conduct:

> مَنْ كَانَتْ لَهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ حَاجَةٌ فَلْيَطْلُبْهَا فِي ثَلَاثِ سَاعَاتٍ: ١- فِي يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ سَاعَةَ زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ ٢- وَحِينَ تَهبُّ الرِّيَاحُ وَتُفْتَحُ أَبْوَابُ السَّمَاءِ وَتَنْزِلُ الرَّحْمَةُ ٣- وَسَاعَةً فِي آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ عِنْدَ طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ.

> وَإِنَّ مَلَكَيْنِ يُنَادِيَانِ هَلْ مِنْ تَائِبٍ فَيُتَابَ عَلَيْهِ هَلْ مِنْ سَائِلٍ فَيُعْطَىٰ هَلْ مِنْ مُسْتَغْفِرٍ فَيُغْفَرَ لَهُ هَلْ مِنْ طَالِبِ حَاجَةٍ فَأَجِيبُوا دَاعِيَ اللَّهِ

Whoever has a need before God, let him seek it in three hours:

1. On the day of Friday, at the hour when the sun passes its zenith.
2. When the winds blow, and the gates of heaven are opened, and mercy descends.
3. An hour at the end of the night, at the breaking of dawn.

He says in it: the supplication of devotion in the Friday prayer falls before the bowing in the second cycle. The recitation on Friday is: in the first cycle, the chapter of the Congregation after the Opening of the Book, and in the second, the Opening of the Book followed by the chapter of the Hypocrites.

He says in it, among legal questions that are all marvels, another question: What do you say of a preacher who was delivering the sermon on Friday when a man entered through the door of the congregational mosque, whereupon the sermon of that preacher was spoiled, and so was the prayer of those who prayed with him? The answer: that preacher is the property of the man who entered through the door of the congregational mosque, for that man had appointed him as his deputy; so when he came in upon him, it was no longer permissible for him to go before his master, nor to lead him in prayer.

### On the Prayer of the Two Festivals

I likewise set down here what is contained in the book of questions and answers mentioned at the outset, arranged according to the order of the chapters of the book *Daaim al-Islam*.

The question: What do you say concerning what has come in the Shariah — that no tashriq is incumbent upon the traveler except in a congregational city? Our master, is what is intended by tashriq here the festival prayer, or not? And whoever forgets one of the magnifications in the festival prayer, or more than one — how should he act?

The answer: It has come in the book *al-Mujzi*, in the section on the ages of camels, cattle, and the like, that there is no tashriq except in a congregational city — that is, no prayer of the two festivals — because the two festival prayers are prayed at the rising of the sun, and the one who prays them is called المشرّق (al-mushriq). And it has come in *Mukhtasar al-Musannaf*: whoever forgets part of the magnification completes it before he bows; and if he has already passed beyond the bowing and is certain of the omission, he performs the two prostrations of forgetfulness.

The question: What do you say concerning the magnification from the day of Arafah to the last of the days of tashriq being twenty-three magnifications, while in our lands they add one magnification after the festival prayer so that it becomes twenty-four? And what is the meaning of this?

The answer: The magnification in those days is twenty-three, and it is a likeness of what obtains in the summons of the five speakers — the possessors of firm resolve — who correspond to the five prayers, drawn from the mention of the ten spiritual ranks and the ten bodily ranks, and the mention of the speaker of the cycle, his executor, and the Imam of the age.

> فَخُذْ مَا أُوتِيتَ وَكُنْ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ

So take what you have been given, and be among the thankful.

From another source: whoever prays the festival prayer while owing a makeup of the dawn prayer, his festival prayer is valid and he does not repeat it; and likewise the funeral prayer.

From our master al-Hasan ibn Idris: whoever prays the festival prayer before bringing out the alms of the breaking of the fast does not repeat it, and he hands over the alms afterward. The washing for the two festivals is a practice of the Prophet. The first of its time is the breaking of dawn, and the last of it is the time of the sun's passing the zenith. Whoever prays the festival prayer before the sun passes the zenith, for an excuse, it is valid for him.

He says in the book *Mukhtasar al-Musannaf*: the washing for the two festivals is a practice of the Prophet; the first of its time is the breaking of dawn and the last of it is the time of the sun's passing the zenith.

He says in the book of reports: and the supplication of devotion is:

> اَللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَارْحَمْنِي وَعَافِنِي وَاعْفُ عَنِّي فِي الدِّينِ وَالدُّنْيَا إِنَّكَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

O God, forgive me, have mercy on me, grant me well-being, and pardon me in religion and in the world. You are powerful over all things.

He says in it: if the people of the desert attend — and those travelers who choose to attend the festival — that is good, and there is merit in it for them. And from it: it is fitting for whoever is among the people of the desert, at two leagues from the city or less, to witness the festival.

He says in it: its congregation is five, one of them the Imam, as with the congregation of the Friday prayer; and where there is one who establishes it, it is an obligation like the obligation of Friday. Whoever misses it with the one who establishes it but catches the two sermons prays it as four as well. Whoever misses one cycle of the festival prayer and catches the second with the Imam adds to it another cycle with its magnifications. The practice regarding the magnification is that it begins after the completion of the fast, on the night of the breaking of the fast and on the day of the breaking of the fast, until he prays and finishes the prayer. Whoever prays the festival prayer raises his hands with every magnification. Whoever forgets part of the magnification completes it before he bows; and if he has passed beyond the bowing and is certain of the omission, he performs the two prostrations of forgetfulness.

He says in the book *al-Musannaf*: the festival prayer is not prayed at Mina. Likewise our master al-Qadi al-Numan ibn Muhammad said in *Tawil al-Daaim*; and it has been verified from our master Idris ibn Hasan that the festival prayer is not prayed there in congregation, but each one prays it by himself, one by one.

He says in the book of questions and answers mentioned at the outset: intercourse with one's wife is permitted on the night of the festival of the breaking of the fast and before the festival prayer.

Our master Jafar ibn Mansur al-Yaman said in the book *al-Rida al-Batin*: it is permitted after the festival of the breaking of the fast to fast on the following day and thereafter. And he says in it: it is not permitted after this festival — meaning the festival of the sacrifice — as it is permitted after the festival of the breaking of the fast.

Our master Zayd ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl said in the *Hidden Epistle*, concerning the prayer of the festival of the breaking of the fast: الفطر (al-fitr) in the language means appearance and beginning. One says تَفَطَّرَتِ الْأَرْضُ وَانْفَطَرَتْ (tafattarat al-ard wa-infatarat) — meaning the earth split open and what lay within it appeared and came forth. Likewise تَفَطَّرَتِ الشَّجَرَةُ (tafattarat al-shajarah) means that its hidden fruit appeared. And فَطَرَ نَابُ الْبَعِيرِ (fatara nab al-bair) means that it came up and appeared. In all these examples there runs a single sense: it is the day on which the command and the things that had been hidden come to light. From this, the breaking of the fast was named fitr, for fasting is silence and concealment. God the Exalted said in the story of Maryam:

> إِنِّى نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ صَوْمًۭا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِنسِيًّۭا

I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful, so I shall not speak to any human being today.

That is: I have vowed silence and stillness, showing nothing of what is within me. So fitr is the appearance of secrets and the knowledge of hidden things. And His saying,

> وإذا السماء انفطرت

And when the sky is split open,

means that it was cleft and what was within it came forth. In another meaning, al-fitr (الْفِطْر) is the new; and فَطَرَ اللَّهُ الْخَلْقَ (fatara Allah al-khalq) means the beginning of His fashioning of them. The day of the breaking of the fast is therefore the day of the manifestation of the command that had been veiled. Then he said: Whoever has fasted the days of the month of Ramadan, for him is the breaking of the fast, the festival, and joy; and whoever does not know the meaning of the reality of fasting and its limits has nothing of God, and he is as God, mighty and majestic, said:

> عَامِلَةٌ نَاصِبَةٌ تَصْلَى نَارًا حَامِيَةً

Toiling, weary, burning in a scorching fire.

The festival prayer has neither a call to prayer nor a call to stand. He then said: the sermon at the breaking of the fast comes after the prayer. He said: the recitation in it is aloud. He said: the prayer of the sacrifice is on the day of the sacrifice — the day of the pilgrimage. He then said: the fact that this sermon begins contrary to all other sermons is a sign that the command appears otherwise than it was in the cycles that have passed. Every sermon begins with praise, except the sermon of the day of the sacrifice, which begins with the four magnifications.

I turn now to the washing of the dead and to what belongs with it.

In the book of questions and answers arranged according to the order of the chapters of *The Pillars of Islam*, the following was asked. Question: what do you say concerning a man who washes the dead? Must he perform the ablution upon them three times together with three washings, or not? Answer: yes, he performs the ablution upon them three times together with three washings; and if he performs their ablution at the last of the washings, that suffices for them, as comes in the Book of Reports. From another place: if a man is wounded and is not moved from his place, and lives an hour, or two hours, or a day, and speaks, he is likewise not washed, because he was not lifted from his place.

Question: concerning one who dies while travelling and no water is to be found; or a man who dies among women with no woman of his own; or a woman who dies with no husband and no woman to be found who may wash her — must the dead in such cases be given tayammum with earth, or not? Answer: it is mentioned that if a man in a state of janabah and a dead person are together, and there is not enough water except for one of them, the man in janabah performs the washing and the dead is given tayammum; and these cases are like that. From another place: if a man dies, the washer washes the dead even while in janabah; and if washing would harm him, he performs tayammum and then washes the dead, and this is permitted when he finds no one else. And if the man in janabah is the more excellent of them, his washing of the dead is permitted.

It is said in the Mukhtasar of al-Musannif that the nearest of those present to the dead has the best right to wash him. From the same book: if the martyr was in janabah, he is washed on account of the janabah. And if a man is found dead with no mark upon him, he is washed, treated with hanut, and shrouded.

It is said in the Mukhtasar al-Athar that the drowned and the burned are washed, and so is a limb — when there is found of a man such a part that it is known he could not have lived once it was parted from him. Whatever falls from the dead is washed and placed with him. If his limbs, or any of them, have come apart, they are washed and each limb is set in its own place, and he is shrouded in that condition and buried. It is said in the Mukhtasar of al-Musannif that no hair is to be shaved from the dead and no nail is to be trimmed.

Our master and lord Jafar, son of our master Sulayman, answered questions put to him by his servant, the author of this book, replying from the island of Yemen to the island of Hind. Among what I asked, I said: what do you say concerning a woman who dies? Is she wrapped in an إزار (izar) and washed as a man is wrapped, or is the end of her wrapper drawn behind her over her private parts and between her thighs until the other end comes round behind her, in the fashion used by the unbelievers and by others among the Muslims? For the Daudi group uses this and denounces whoever does not use it. Is that to be used when she is washed, or not? And is her wrapper to be so arranged in her shrouding, or not? For the Daudi group for the most part uses it in shrouding. They likewise use a ستارة (sitarah) when the dead is washed, screening the body from the women. Is nothing else permitted, or is there no harm in her being washed without a screen over her when she is at a distance from men?

The answer to that: nothing is mentioned in the book of the Pillars except that an izar is placed upon the dead when he is washed, reaching from the navel to the knees, and the water is passed beneath it, and the washer wraps a cloth upon his hand and brings it in under the izar and washes the private parts and the rest of the 'awrah that lies beneath the izar. Practice rests upon that, and the manner you have described prevents its being done. The shrouding is likewise, and concerning it there has come in the book *The Pillars of Islam*, from Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع), that he said:

> نِعْمَ الْكَفَنُ ثَلَاثَةُ أَثْوَابٍ قَمِيصٌ غَيْرُ مَزْرُورٍ وَلَا مَكْفُوفٍ وَلِفَافَةٌ وَاِزَارٌ

The best shroud is three garments: a shirt neither buttoned nor hemmed, a wrapping sheet, and a waist wrapper. Know that. As for the matter of the screen in the washing of the dead — and above all of a woman — the better course is that it be done only within a covering.

And of what I asked, I said: what do you say concerning the meaning of the words of our master al-Qadi al-Numan ibn Muhammad in the Book of Purity, at the end of it, in the mention of the washing of the dead, where he says that the woman is bound up and is given the 'ajrah? What is the meaning of his word وتعجر? The answer to that: the عجرة (جُرْح) known in the lands of the Arabs, spelled with the undotted راء (ra'), is the gathering of the shirt, drawing together that part of it which faces the navel down to below the navel over the clothing, and tucking it into the fastening of the izar. That is a mark of difference between men and women, like the head covering which is a mark of difference between men and women. Know that.

Our lord the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (ع), said in his Four Hundred Counsels:

> مَنْ مَسَّ جَسَدَ الْمَيِّتِ بَعْدَ مَا بَرَدَ فَعَلَيْهِ الْغُسْلُ

Whoever touches the body of الميت after it has grown cold — برد جسد — must perform the washing.

And he said in it:

> مَنْ غَسَّلَ مَيِّتًا فَلْيَغْتَسِلْ بَعْدَ مَا يُلْبِسُهُ الْكَفَنَ وَلَا يَمَسَّهُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَيَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ الْغُسْلُ

In the book of questions and answers already mentioned, I find this saying explained. Question: what do you say concerning the meaning of the words of the Commander of the Faithful (ع) — that whoever touches the body of the dead after it grows cold is bound to perform the washing? What is the meaning of "after it grows cold"? Answer: it means after his end has come upon him and he has been washed according to the sunnah by whoever washes him, because the body of the dead has become impure; when its moisture reaches a living man it renders him impure, and that is the meaning of the washing being binding upon him.

In the book of questions sent by certain dignitaries of Hind, answered by certain of our lords the summoners in the Yemeni peninsula, I find it written: you asked about a woman who gave birth to two children joined to one another — what is to be done with them, and if one of them dies, what is to be done with him. God, mighty and exalted, creates what He wills. If their adhesion is such that separation is possible, what lies between them is cut without harm to them and without danger, when the matter is slight; but if it is grave and dangerous, they are left as they are. In that case their death is one death and their life is one life, and God knows best, and He does what He wills. If one of them dies and not the other, whatever adheres to the living one is cut from the dead one, as long as the living one feels no sensation or pain from the cutting, if that is possible; the dead one is buried and the living one is left. But if pain is felt in the body of the other, then their life is but one life and their death but one death, and God knows best.

As for the hanut and the shroud, I find it asked in the same book: what do you say concerning what comes in the Book of Reports — that the first thing taken from the estate of the dead is the shroud and his outfitting, then the debt, then the bequest? O our master, if the debt is greater than his estate, is his outfitting to be taken from it according to his station, even if it is costly? Answer: his shroud and his outfitting must be taken out according to his station.

From another place: the hanut is placed upon the places of prostration of the dead, and upon the private parts and the feet, and between the thumb and the forefinger, and upon the navel, the armpits, the breast, the mouth, the eyes, the nose, the forehead, the ears, and the hands at the palms, and the knees. A little oil, wheat, and perfume are put into the water on the third night, and the water is poured upon the grave on the third day. If the dead man is of the people of rank, the Quran is recited over his grave for seven days, and over the graves of others for three days; such has been the practice of our lords, may God lengthen their lives. It has come from our master Hasan ibn Idris that the Quran is recited for the people of rank seven times and for others three times, whether in the mosque, at the graves, in the house, or elsewhere.

In the Mukhtasar al-Athar, I find that the hanut is whatever is of perfume, but neither wars nor saffron is put into the hanut of men, while these are put into the hanut of women. In the Book of Purity, I find that the hanut and the camphor are placed upon the forehead and the nose, the insides of the palms, the knees, and the tops of the feet — these being the places of prostration. From the same book: cotton is placed upon the face, under the armpits, and between the knees, the shins, and the feet, if it is to be had.

In the Tawil al-Daaim, I find that the sunnah concerning the incensing of the dead is this: the dead man himself is not incensed, nor is his bier followed with incense; rather his shroud is incensed, and the place in which he is washed and shrouded — and nothing beyond that. And our lord the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (ع), said in his Four Hundred Counsels:

> وَلَا تُجَمِّرُوا مَوْتَاكُمْ وَلَا تَمَسُّوهُمْ بِالطِّيبِ اِلَّا بِالْكَافُورِ فَاِنَّ الْمَيِّتَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْمُحْرِمِ

Do not perfume your dead with incense, and do not touch them with any fragrance except camphor, for the dead man is in the position of one consecrated for pilgrimage.

In a book of legal questions, all of them remarkable, I find another question: what do you say concerning a man who died, whose head and face were not covered and to whom nothing of the hanut was brought near when he died and was shrouded? Answer: that man died as a pilgrim in a state of consecration, so his head and his face are not covered, and nothing of perfume is brought near him, because he is consecrated during days that are numbered.

As for walking with the bier, I find it asked in the same book: what do you say concerning what comes in the law commanding that one walk behind the bier? O our master, does a man sin if he walks before it, or not? Answer: it is mentioned in the Book of Reports that walking is disliked only before the bier of an enemy of the family, because of the angels of wrath that come to it. As for the believers, it matters not where you walk in relation to the bier, since the angels of mercy encompass it. Yet walking behind it is the more excellent. I find it stated in the Book of Reports that they disliked the call to prayer at the bier, and permitted the informing of people of the death without a public call.

In the Tawil al-Daaim, I find that what is required is this: no one should rise for the bier when it passes except one who intends to follow it, and he should not sit down until it has been set at the edge of the grave. From the Mukhtasar al-Athar: when the dead is brought to the burial ground, the bier is set down crosswise, the dead lying upon his back upon it, so that his right side is toward the qibla and his left toward the one who prays.

From the Tawil al-Daaim, and of that is what is related of the Messenger of God (ع):

> نَظَرَ إِلَى النِّسَاءِ يَتْبَعْنَ جَنَازَةً فَوَقَفَ وَقَالَ لَهُنَّ تُصَلِّينَ عَلَيْهَا فِي مَنْ يُصَلِّي قُلْنَ لَا قَالَ فَتَحْمِلْنَهَا فِي مَنْ يَحْمِلُهَا قُلْنَ لَا قَالَ فَتَنْزِلْنَ لَهَا فِي الْقَبْرِ فِي مَنْ يَنْزِلُهَا قُلْنَ لَا قَالَ فَتُوَارِينَهَا فِي مَنْ يُوَارِيهَا قُلْنَ لَا قَالَ فَارْجِعْنَ مَعْذُورَاتٍ غَيْرَ مَأْجُورَاتٍ

The *Mukhtasar al-Athar* records that we have transmitted from the Imams of the household of the Messenger of God (ع) that they commanded the following: once the deceased has been shrouded, he is placed upon his bier and laid upon it, when a bier is to be had and this is possible; men carry him on their shoulders, when men can be found. If that is not possible, he is carried on a beast or by whatever other means are available. His shroud is covered from above with a cloth, if one is to be had. A canopy is erected over the bier and it is screened with a cloth; and the deceased is secured if there is fear he may fall from the bier.

On the prayer over the dead, the same book was asked: What do you say concerning a man who dies in a place where no authorized man is present, though an authorized woman is? May she lead the women in the funeral prayer, or should the men pray over him individually and he then be buried? Answer: The prayer of a man is more in keeping with the teaching of the People of the House (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ).

Question: What of the prayer over the dead — is it permitted to pray over him after he has been carried from the place where he was prepared, or not until he reaches the burial ground? Answer: He may be prayed over wherever one wishes: in the burial ground, in his house, or anywhere else. Whoever wishes may recite the supplication between the takbirs of the funeral prayer; whoever wishes may leave it and be content with the imam. The funeral prayer is also permitted during the disliked hours and at the time of an eclipse.

The *Majalis al-Bayan* states that the funeral prayer is a communal obligation upon every Muslim who knows of it, until one of them has performed it, after which the rest participate as volunteers. The Reports record, on the authority of transmitters from the People of the House (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), that it is recommended to pray over the bier within the appointed prayer times, provided there is no risk of missing the prescribed prayer; if that risk exists, one begins with the prescribed prayer.

The *Tawil al-Daaim* likewise states: when the imam of the age is absent, whoever has been appointed judge by him, or given charge by him of some affair of the Muslims, has the better right to the prayer over the dead. If a company of those brought near by the imam's command is present, or of those whom the imam has advanced, the right belongs to the highest among them in station; if only one such person is present, he has a better right to the prayer than the deceased's guardian, being someone the imam has set up, or set up for some affair of the Muslims. Whoever is appointed to lead the people in prayer, if he is present at the bier, has the better right to pray over it. If none of these persons is present, then the most entitled of the guardians has the best right to pray over it.

The *Mukhtasar al-Athar* further states that the funeral prayer is offered over the martyr, over those who have committed grave sins and offenses, and over one killed in execution of a prescribed punishment or in retaliation. The *Mukhtasar* of al-Musannif adds that the supplication is recited quietly during a daytime funeral prayer and aloud during a nighttime one, and that the prayer is offered over one who has taken his own life. From the same book: the deceased's knots are loosened, his right hand is brought out from beneath his side, and his cheek is laid against the earth. If a woman dies carrying a child of six months or more in her womb, the child is taken out if that is possible.

Our master and lord Jafar ibn Sulayman — in his answers to questions put to him by his servant, the author of this book, replying from the island of Yemen to the island of Hind — answered what I asked when I said: What do you say concerning a bier at which one is present, when the imam has come forward to pray over it? Is his recitation of the supplication in the prayer sufficient, or ought the one who follows him to recite it himself as well, given that it is by day? The answer to that: it has come in the book of legal questions and answers that whoever wishes may recite the supplication between the takbirs of the funeral prayer, and whoever wishes may leave it and be content with the imam's recitation. Know that.

As for burial and the graves, it was asked in the same book: What do you say concerning what the law stipulates — that whatever falls from a man while he is alive is to be buried in the earth? O our master, may he bury it wherever he wishes, or only in the burial ground? And if he leaves it and does not bury it, does he sin in that or not? Answer: He buries it wherever he wishes, and there is no blame upon him if it is lost.

Question: What do you say concerning a man in whose land people have buried their dead without his leave, and who, when he came to know of it, wished to have them removed? Is that permitted to him or not? Answer: It is not permitted that burial be made in his land except with his leave; but since they did that without his consent, he has nothing but the value of the places of the graves, and it is not permitted to him to have them removed.

Question: What do you say concerning what the law commands — the burial of the dead where they fell and the prohibition of moving them? O our master, if the burial ground is far off, how is one to act? Answer: The deceased is buried in the place where he dies, in the burial ground of the people of that town, and he is not to be carried to another town. But if he dies in open wilderness, there is no harm in his being carried to the nearest burial ground.

Question: What do you say concerning a woman who dies when there is not to be found in the town any male relative who may lawfully look upon her? Who shall lower her into the grave? Answer: If a woman dies and no kinsman to whom looking upon her is lawful is present at her grave, then the person nearest to her undertakes the burial; and if such a one is lacking, upright men other than her kin bury her out of necessity.

Question: What do you say concerning what comes in the books of the rightly guiding summons — that mud bricks, wood, or whatever else one wishes are placed over the dead, and that if earth is heaped over him it is well? O our master, is it permitted to place over him baked brick, stone, and whatever else is to be found? For the people of the outward sense dislike baked brick. How does the matter stand — may God make us your ransom? Answer: It is permitted to place over him baked brick and whatever else is to be found. Rely upon this and pay no regard to anything else, save what may be done for prudent concealment.

And our lord the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (ع), said in his Four Hundred Counsels:

> أَلِمُّوا بِالْقُبُورِ الَّتِي يَلْزَمُكُمْ حَقُّ سُكَّانِهَا وَزُورُوهَا وَاطْلُبُوا الرِّزْقَ عِنْدَهَا فَأِنَّهُمْ يَفْرَحُونَ بِزِيَارَتِكُمْ وَلْيَطْلُبِ الرَّجُلُ الْحَاجَةَ عِنْدَ قَبْرِ أَبِيهِ وَأُمِّهِ بَعْدَ مَا يَدْعُو لَهُمَا

Visit the graves of those who have a claim upon you. Go to them, and seek provision at their graves, for they rejoice at your visiting. Let a man ask for what he needs at the grave of his father and his mother, after he has prayed for them both.

I turn now to zakat al-fitr.

In the first book of questions and answers — arranged according to the chapter order of the Book of the Pillars of Islam — the following exchange appears. Question: the custom among the Indians when collecting the fitra is to mix four kinds of grain — rice, maize, wheat, and salt — and then take their monetary value, whereas in the radiant Shariah the zakat of Fitr is a sa of dates, raisins, wheat, or barley. Does it suffice a person who gives a sa of barley? Answer: the reliance is on what is stated in the Pillars — that is, a sa of wheat, barley, dates, or raisins.

> وَالْفِطْرَةُ مِنْ أَطْيَبِ مَا تَأْكُلُونَ وَأَزْكَى مَا تَدَّخِرُونَ

The fitra is to be from the best of what you eat and the purest of what you store away.

Whoever mixes the fitra from everything he ate during Ramadan, that suffices him; and whoever ate nothing but barley, that too suffices him. Verify this well.

Question: what is the ruling for a man who wishes to pay his fitra before Ramadan begins, fearing that poverty or travel may prevent him from paying it at its proper time? What does the noble law say on this — does it suffice him or not? The question arises because obligatory duties may not be performed outside their appointed times, nor made up except after those times have passed. And if it does not suffice him, it should be noted that the Book of the Pillars states there is no harm in collecting zakat from those who owe it before its due time, when there is need for that. Please provide the answer on this, and also address the case of one who did this out of ignorance — has it sufficed him? Answer: if he delivers his fitra to someone who has the right to receive it, it has sufficed him. The prohibition in this matter is that a person should not break his fast before delivering his fitra. No fixed time was set for advancing or delaying it; the obligation is simply its delivery.

He stated in the book Mukhtasar al-Musannaf: a dhimmi who accepts Islam before the break of dawn on the day of Fitr owes the zakat of Fitr; if he accepts Islam after the break of dawn, nothing is due from him.

He stated in the reports: they narrated that the zakat of Fitr is paid on behalf of the mukatab. He stated in the Landmarks of Religion: if a child is born before the break of dawn on the day of Fitr, the zakat of Fitr is due on his behalf. He stated in the Book of the Pillars: it has likewise been said that it is paid on behalf of the child still in his mother's womb, before birth. He stated in the Selected Book: or a sa of dried curd, or half a sa of wheat. He stated in the Landmarks of Religion that the weight of the sa is four and a half ratls by the ratl of Mecca; he stated therein that its weight by the ratl of Medina is five ratls less a third of a ratl; and its weight by the Baghdadi ratl is nine ratls and a tenth of a ratl.

Our master and lord, the author of the Mustansiriyya sessions — peace of God be upon him — stated in the thirteenth session: since we mentioned in the session before this one the zakat that is obligatory upon those who possess wealth, we follow that with the mention of the zakat that is obligatory in every condition, and upon those of small means who give it in charity — and that is the zakat of Fitr. In it are seven obligations and twelve practices of the Sunnah. The obligations are:

1. that a man pay it on behalf of himself;
2. on behalf of the elder of his household;
3. and the younger of them;
4. and the free among them;
5. and the enslaved among them;
6. and the males among them;
7. and the females among them.

The practices of the Sunnah are that he bring it out from the middle sort of what he eats — a sa of wheat, or a sa of barley, or a sa of dates, or a sa of raisins; half a sa of wheat suffices him, and from anything other than wheat nothing suffices but a full sa; and the sa is four mudds. He should hand it to the Imam (ع), or to whomever the Imam has appointed; it should be brought out before the breaking of the fast; whoever delays bringing it out must make it up; and whoever lacks the food brings out its value in silver or in gold. As for the woman who has no husband with her, she brings it out on behalf of herself and on behalf of those she supports.

He stated in the book of the Inner Nursing, regarding the saying of the Messenger of God:

> اَلْفِطْرَةُ لَا تَحِلُّ لِي وَلَا لِأَهْلِ بَيْتِي

The fitra is not lawful for me, nor for the people of my house.

Our master Zayd ibn Muhammad — may God sanctify his spirit — stated in the Concealed Epistle: as for the charity of Fitr, the Messenger of God made it obligatory upon every head among the Muslims to pay his fitra — upon the males and the females, the small and the great, even the infant born on that very day — and it is paid on behalf of the child in his mother's womb. He made obligatory upon every head a sa of wheat, dates, raisins, barley, or other grains. He stated therein:

> وَسُمِّيَتْ صَدَقَةُ الْفِطْرِ صَدَقَةَ الرَّأْسِ

The charity of Fitr has been named the charity of the head.

He stated therein: it is paid before the prayer, and if it is paid before the prayer it is charity. He stated therein: if the child is born after the Fitr, the fitra is paid before the Fitr.

He stated in the book Mafatih al-Nima — which belongs to our master the Judge al-Numan ibn Muhammad, may God exalt his sanctity — concerning the fitra:

> فَاِنْ أُخْرِجَتْ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ كَانَتْ فِطْرَةً وَإِذَا أُخْرِجَتْ بَعْدَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ كَانَتْ صَدَقَةً

If it is brought out before sunrise, it counts as fitra; if it is brought out after sunrise, it is ordinary charity.

He stated, up to his words:

> وَمَعْنَى الْفِطْرَةِ إِخْرَاجُ الْوَاجِبِ لِلَّهِ وَلِوَلِيِّهِ مِنَ الْفِكَاكِ وَالْقُرْبَانِ

The meaning of fitra is the bringing out of what is owed to God and to His appointed guardian, as ransom and as offering.

I turn now to various rulings on zakat, on the one upon whom no zakat falls, and on other matters. In a book of legal questions — each one a marvel — he raised another question: what do you say concerning a man for whom the zakat on his wealth has been made lawful? The answer: in that case he is a man who owns a thousand dinars and owes a thousand dinars, so there is no zakat upon him on it. He stated therein another question: what do you say concerning a man for whom the zakat on his wealth is lawful while he himself is well off? The answer: in that case he is a man among the polytheists who has found no Muslim to whom to hand the zakat of his wealth, so he has more right to it than anyone else.
